record.paper_title: Open problems in membrane computing and how not to solve them
record.original_question: Do polynomial-time uniform and semi-uniform families of sufficiently powerful P systems, such as standard P systems with active membranes, recognize the same decision languages? In the semi-uniform setting, a polynomial-time Turing machine M receives the entire input string x and outputs an encoding of a recogniser P system Pi_x; in the uniform setting, one polynomial-time machine F receives only n = |x| and builds a skeleton Pi_n valid for every input of that length, while another polynomial-time machine E receives x and produces an input multiset w that is placed into Pi_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider P systems with active membranes used as recognisers of decision languages over a finite alphabet Σ. A recogniser P system halts on every input and signals acceptance or rejection by sending a distinguished object out of the skin membrane.

A semi-uniform family {Π_x}_{x∈Σ*} is one for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine M running in time polynomial in |x| that, on input x, outputs an encoding of a recogniser P system Π_x whose computations accept iff x belongs to the language.

A uniform family {Π_n, w_x} is specified by two deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines:
 • F, which on input 1^n outputs an encoding of a "skeleton" P system Π_n depending only on the length n = |x|;
 • E, which on input x outputs a multiset w_x of objects that is placed into a designated input region of Π_{|x|}.
The combined system Π_n with initial multiset w_x augmented decides membership of x in the language.

Let PMC_AM (resp. PMC*_AM) denote the class of languages decidable by polynomial-time uniform (resp. semi-uniform) families of P systems with active membranes (with the standard rule set: object evolution, communication, dissolution, and elementary and non-elementary membrane division, with electrical charges).

Question: Is PMC_AM = PMC*_AM? More generally, for "sufficiently powerful" variants of recogniser P systems, do polynomial-time uniform and polynomial-time semi-uniform families recognise exactly the same class of decision languages?
artifact.status_search_result: For weak variants (e.g., AC0-uniform active membrane systems without charges and without dissolution), strict separations between uniform and semi-uniform classes are known: (AC0)-PMC_AM0−d ⊊ (AC0,AC0)-PMC*_AM0−d = NL. For the full polynomial-time uniform vs. semi-uniform question with standard P systems with active membranes (with charges and division), the problem appears to remain open in the membrane computing literature.

status_evidence.title: Uniformity conditions for membrane systems: Uncovering complexity below P
status_evidence.snippet: AC0-uniform families of active membrane systems without charges and dissolution characterise a strict subset of their semi-uniform equivalent.
status_evidence.claim: Separation between uniform and semi-uniform is known for weak (AC0-uniform, no charges, no dissolution) variants.

status_evidence.title: Uniformity: uncovering the frontier of parallelism
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniformity vs. semi-uniformity frontiers for membrane systems.
status_evidence.claim: Uniformity vs. semi-uniformity questions for P systems are an active research direction with known separations at weak levels.
